raw_entries.description: The Jewish Essene sect of ascetics saw the Jewish uprising against the Romans in 66–70 in Judea as the final end-time battle which would bring about the arrival of the Messiah. By the authority of Simon, coins were minted declaring the redemption of Israel.
raw_entries.summary_de: Typ: religioeses Endzeitszenario. Behaupteter Zeitpunkt des Endes: 66-70. Im Eintrag als Urheber oder Verfechter benannt: Simon bar Giora, Jewish Essenes. Die Ankunft des Messias wird als Schluessel des Endes genannt. Der juedische Aufstand gegen Rom in Judaea wird als letzte Endzeitschlacht gelesen. Sogar gepraegte Muenzen sollten die behauptete Erloesung sichtbar bezeugen. Das Ende wird als finale Schlacht oder letzte Gewaltzuspitzung gedacht. Die englische Quellbeschreibung bleibt im Datensatz erhalten und enthaelt weitere Originaldetails.
raw_entries.radio_hook_de: Als Traeger der Endzeitprognose erscheint Simon bar Giora, Jewish Essenes; der angesetzte Termin ist 66-70.

raw_entries.description: The 2012 phenomenon predicted the world would end at the end of the 13th b'ak'tun. Scientists from NASA, along with expert archeologists, stated that none of those events were possible.

raw_entries.description: The "Toledo Letter", purportedly from a group of Spanish astrologers, claimed that an incoming planetary conjunction on 15 September 1186 would trigger a series of natural disasters that would wipe out all life. While the conjunction did occur, the predicted apocalypse did not follow: in fact, the night of September 15 was noted to be unusually calm. Variants of the same letter continued to surface over the next few centuries with only the names and dates changed, predicting identical cataclysms.

raw_entries.description: In or around 1214, somebody claiming to be "Cardinal Johannes Toletanus" warned that the end of the world was coming. The pamphlet which carried his warning was later identified as a variant of the above-mentioned Toledo letter being used yet again. The dates had been altered, predicting the apocalypse in 1229 instead of 1186, but the content was almost identical to the previous hoax, even citing the exact same conjunction as the cause of the disaster. People still fell for it.

raw_entries.description: The Great Flood of 1524 was predicted for February 4 which would coincide with a conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn, predicted by several astrologers including Johann Stöffler in 1499 and Johannes Carion in 1521. It was popularised by a vast number of pamphlets in the early 16th century, which has led to it being described as the first mass-media panic in history. Many people feared the worst, building boats and moving to higher ground; nothing happened, and in London, where some of the most extreme panic had manifested, it didn't even rain.

raw_entries.description: The presence of the Number of the Beast in this date meant many people assumed it would see the end of the world, with outbreaks of bubonic plague in the years before adding to millenarian feeling. The |, a millenarian English sect that sprung up during the English Civil War, believed the world would end in 1666 or before. They were influential in the radical politics of the 1650s and tried to set up a council of saints to form the fifth monarchy (following the Babylonian, Persian, Macedonian, and Roman) which they predicted would bring the end of the world, based on Daniel 2:37–44. But the Restoration of Charles II reduced their influence, and even plague and fire couldn't help.

raw_entries.description: Dr. M.H. Kahn believes that all of all other predictions in the past are invalid. He writes: ::"The contraction of the universe with reversal of time and gravity will commence the beginning of the end which will last for thousands and possibly millions of years. raw_entries.description: According to current models, the Sun is expected to increase in luminosity by 10% in the next 500 million years before fading out and dying. This will cause several changes to the climate that will make the continued existence of life on Earth impossible, starting with photosynthetic organisms and eventually killing off all life. During the period of the next 500 million years, there is a small chance that a passing star will throw Earth out of orbit, causing catastrophic events from burning, freezing or collision.

raw_entries.description: The Andromeda Galaxy (currently 2.5 million light years away) has about a 50% chance (by 2025 estimates) of colliding and merging with our galaxy, the Milky Way. This is unlikely to have much of an effect on whatever life is around, as galaxies are mostly empty space, although for any given planet, there is a tiny chance that its orbit could be disrupted due to gravitational tugs from passing stars. The other 50% chance is that two other galaxies in our Local Group, the Large Magellanic Cloud and Messier 33 will prevent the merger.

raw_entries.description: According to accepted models of stellar evolution, the Sun will run out of hydrogen in its core to fuse into helium and will transition to a red giant as a result, expanding massively. The Sun will swallow Mercury and Venus, and may get large enough to swallow Earth as well. Even if it doesn't, Earth will be roasted to a cinder crisp. One school of thought predicts that the drag from the Sun's outer gas envelope will cause the Earth to spiral into the Sun, but as with all things scientific, there is another school of thought that says this won't happen. If it isn't swallowed, Earth will either get flung out into interstellar space due to tidal interactions with the Sun and the Sun's gradual loss of mass once it enters the red giant stage or will keep orbiting the dead Sun, perhaps reduced just to its core, for a long time to come. Never again will Earth see another day.

raw_entries.description: estimated maximum time for all nucleons in the observable universe to decay, if protons are unstable. Whether they are is currently an unresolved question in physics. Exasecond and longer and Future of an expanding universe have a pile of similarly apocalyptic events that actually have some scientific basis. This is the Total Existence Failure of the entire universe; anything complex enough to be considered life that would care about it would likely have evaporated to nothing long before this. Out of all the above, this is the most likely.

raw_entries.description: The heat death of the universe ("Big Freeze") is a scientific prediction that eventually the universe will expand so much it will no longer contain any thermodynamic free energy with which to do work. At this point the universe will be cold, dark, and essentially empty forever. That is, unless quantum fluctuations or some other phenomena eventually cause something to occur, like a new Big Bang. Forever is a long time, and this kind of physics is poorly understood at present.

scenarios.canonical_title: Stephen A. Nelson – Weltuntergang für < 100 million
scenarios.summary_de: Typ: astronomisch-astrologisches Weltuntergangsszenario. Behaupteter Zeitpunkt des Endes: unter 100 Millionen Jahren. Im Eintrag als Urheber oder Verfechter benannt: Stephen A. Nelson. Als Ausloeser wird ein Asteroideneinschlag genannt. Der beschriebene Einschlag koennte von einem Himmelskoerper mit etwa 10 bis 15 Kilometern Durchmesser ausgehen. Als Vergleich dient das Aussterbeereignis, das auch die Dinosaurier ausloeschte. Die englische Quellbeschreibung bleibt im Datensatz erhalten und enthaelt weitere Originaldetails.
scenarios.radio_hook_de: Als Traeger der Endzeitprognose erscheint Stephen A. Nelson; der angesetzte Termin ist unter 100 Millionen Jahren.

descriptions: It is estimated that every 100 million years, Earth will be hit by an asteroid about 10–15 km in diameter, comparable in size to the one that triggered the K–Pg extinction which killed dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

descriptions: In approximately 300,000 years, WR 104, a triple star, is expected to explode in a supernova. It has been suggested that it may produce a gamma ray burst that could pose a threat to life on Earth should its poles be aligned 12° or lower towards Earth. However, spectroscopic observations now strongly suggest that it is tilted at an angle of 30°-40° and so any gamma ray burst should not hit Earth.

descriptions: By this time it is estimated that a gamma ray burst, or massive, hyperenergetic supernova, would have occurred within 6,500 light-years of Earth; close enough for its rays to affect Earth's ozone layer and potentially trigger a mass extinction, assuming the hypothesis is correct that a previous such explosion triggered the Ordovician–Silurian extinction event. However, the supernova would have to be precisely oriented relative to Earth to have any negative effect.

descriptions: Muslims believed in the Qiyamah (Last Judgement), during which time Jesus will come to earth, end all wars, and kill ad-Dajjal — the Muslim antichrist. Then every person who ever lived will be bodily resurrected, before being judged by God. The faithful go to heaven, and the rest to hell. Apparently there's also room for some "People of the Book," i.e. Jews and Christians, though hopefully there won't be any wars between the lot in heaven. Presumably God will actually do something to stop fighting within his heavenly realm, unlike on Earth, so that celestial wars would seem unlikely.

descriptions: The "Toledo Letter", purportedly from a group of Spanish astrologers, claimed that an incoming planetary conjunction on 15 September 1186 would trigger a series of natural disasters that would wipe out all life. Variants of the same letter continued to surface over the next few centuries with only the names and dates changed, predicting identical cataclysms.

descriptions: The presence of the Number of the Beast in this date meant many people assumed it would see the end of the world, with outbreaks of bubonic plague in the years before adding to millenarian feeling. The |, a millenarian English sect that sprung up during the English Civil War, believed the world would end in 1666 or before. They were influential in the radical politics of the 1650s and tried to set up a council of saints to form the fifth monarchy (following the Babylonian, Persian, Macedonian, and Roman) which they predicted would bring the end of the world, based on Daniel 2:37–44. But the Restoration of Charles II reduced their influence, and even plague and fire couldn't help.

The Earth would be destroyed by an asteroid, Nibiru, or some other interplanetary object; an alien invasion; or a supernova. Mayanist scholars stated that no extant classic Maya accounts forecasted impending doom, and that the idea that the Long Count calendar ends in 2012 misrepresented Maya history and culture. Scientists from NASA, along with expert archeologists, stated that none of those events were possible.

descriptions: According to accepted models of stellar evolution, the Sun will run out of hydrogen in its core to fuse into helium and will transition to a red giant as a result, expanding massively. The Sun will swallow Mercury and Venus, and may get large enough to swallow Earth as well. Even if it doesn't, Earth will be roasted to a cinder crisp. One school of thought predicts that the drag from the Sun's outer gas envelope will cause the Earth to spiral into the Sun, but as with all things scientific, there is another school of thought that says this won't happen. If it isn't swallowed, Earth will either get flung out into interstellar space due to tidal interactions with the Sun and the Sun's gradual loss of mass once it enters the red giant stage or will keep orbiting the dead Sun, perhaps reduced just to its core, for a long time to come. Never again will Earth see another day.

descriptions: A hypothetical dark companion star, Nemesis, with an eccentric orbit of about 27 million years, triggers periodic mass extinctions by perturbing objects beyond Neptune into hitting the Earth. Arguments against say it is a statistical artifact and sky surveys have failed to find it.

descriptions: The Andromeda Galaxy (currently 2.5 million light years away) has about a 50% chance (by 2025 estimates) of colliding and merging with our galaxy, the Milky Way. This is unlikely to have much of an effect on whatever life is around, as galaxies are mostly empty space, although for any given planet, there is a tiny chance that its orbit could be disrupted due to gravitational tugs from passing stars. The other 50% chance is that two other galaxies in our Local Group, the Large Magellanic Cloud and Messier 33 will prevent the merger.

descriptions: The heat death of the universe ("Big Freeze") is a scientific prediction that eventually the universe will expand so much it will no longer contain any thermodynamic free energy with which to do work. At this point the universe will be cold, dark, and essentially empty forever. That is, unless quantum fluctuations or some other phenomena eventually cause something to occur, like a new Big Bang. Forever is a long time, and this kind of physics is poorly understood at present.
